rows.note: lowercase 'pass' IS a pass - the bug that stalled every wave
uppercase PASS is a pass
'PASS (with notes)' is a pass
'FAIL' is not a pass
'NO-GO' is NEVER read as GO - its first token is NO-GO
and neither is 'no-go'
'GO' is GO
and so is 'go'
a null verdict is not a pass
a null verdict is not a GO
an empty verdict is not a GO
the token itself, so a disagreement points at the splitter
the hyphen stays inside the token - that is what keeps NO-GO out of GO
null yields the empty token, never the string 'null'
leading punctuation is not a token
isRejected reads the same way
'ok' is not a rejection
state strings are compared normalised, never raw
a null state is the empty string, not 'null'
a comma inside a single term is detected
a normal term carries no comma
two terms quote as TWO arguments, not one joined string
an apostrophe is doubled - the only escape a single-quoted PS string has
three elements, one of them carrying commas - the PS 5.1 collection rule says fixtures over collections use at least three
an empty term is dropped rather than quoted into an empty argument
a slug carries its retries across DIFFERENT batch shapes, and retries are per STAGE - the two halves of B6's 657 failed calls
four failures do not trip the breaker
a success resets the streak, so per-recipe flakiness never trips it
five consecutive failures trip the breaker - a wall, not flakiness
the call budget trips before a runaway loop can eat the run
under budget, the breaker stays shut
an explicit trip opens it without any failure at all
clean recipes are NOT held hostage by a blocked neighbour, and the blocker goes back for its one repair
after its repair cycle a blocker is terminal, never re-repaired
an all-blocked wave publishes NOTHING
the per-slug verdict is matched on the BLOCK prefix, case-insensitively
a slug the auditor said nothing about is clean, not blocked
shared-data blockers force a whole-wave re-audit
recipe-local blockers scope to the repaired slugs only
an empty repair list cannot justify a narrow scope
a narrow scope on a shared-data fix is ILLEGAL
whole-wave is always legal
and a shared-data-sized audit of a local fix is merely expensive, not illegal
a repair claiming a file it never touched is refused
a real repair passes
'nothing needed changing' is a legitimate answer, treated differently from a false claim
one untouched file among three is still caught
below the floor fails
above the CEILING fails - a band has two edges
over the carb limit fails
mid-band passes
the exact edges are inside the band
an unreported macro is not a band failure - the band gate rules on numbers, and a missing number is a different problem for a different stage
takeBatch sweeps what is queued without waiting to fill
a closed empty channel returns null rather than hanging
a lone item is taken alone, immediately - streaming, not batching (B3 cost 8-10 minutes to the first flowing recipe)
close() releases a producer parked on backpressure - the hang bug itself
items pushed before close are drained, not discarded
